source: phase-2 slice-12 root (review V20, refute8b, db9a, pw9)
title: DEC-246: Wave-9 rulings on read deadlines, retired rows, re-check announcements, digest-409 copy and evidence stand-ins (2026-10-31)
text:
- **Problem**: review V20, refute8b, lane db9a and lane pw9 asked root for readings before wave 9.
- **Options considered**: per item, the stricter cell vs leaving the state as built; for evidence, citing a stand-in vs not.
- **Decision** (root, owner may override): (1) every CMS browser read takes one shared 8,000 ms deadline (apps/web/src/lib/read-deadline.ts, the value the related-content and locale reads already used); on expiry the island shows its failed/degraded cell with its retry control, never a frozen send (V20 m1/m10); (2) composition keepRetired keeps only rows of the current draft revision (V20 m3); (3) a repeated failed re-check announces a sentence that differs from the previous one (V20 m5); (4) the digest-409 copy says the block choices were read again and the values are kept, never Reload (V20 M1); (5) the composition placement digest 409 re-reads what went stale, like the designers (V20 m9, sibling of DEC-245(1)); (6) AC-294: db9a U1 (real CMS-03A-17 revocation, the create waits at position 1) is citable; U2 (hand-held single-assignment revoke at position 2) is a stand-in with no production writer and is not cited (DEC-245(7)); the part "visibility" stays uncited while no archive writer exists; (7) AC-273 server logs: the real-route harness Worker logger was a no-op — a harness-only gap, closed by capturing the production logger and both wrangler outputs (lane pwfix9), not a BOUNDARY.
- **Downstream**: lanes web9a/web9b; apply8/apply9; AC-271, AC-294, AC-273 limitations.
- **Reversibility**: High

source: phase-2 slice-12 root (lane db9b RED, AC-211)
title: DEC-247: Pattern depth and node bounds re-proved before publish and at placement (2026-10-31)
text:
- **Problem**: lane db9b RED: the cms.pattern.active_digest provider passed a live use reaching ten nested levels or 544 expanded roots, and CMS-03C-02 placed the ten-level pattern (only a 128-level runaway guard), although BE03c 1678 requires the depth/node counts "before save and again before publish" and BE03c 388/1694 require them at placement; BE03c 1585 named no provider reason for them.
- **Options considered**: A re-prove the CMS-03C-12 bounds in the provider and at placement with the existing tokens; B provider only; C accept as designed (no producible production row) and amend BE03c 1678.
- **Decision** (root, owner may override): A. The spec already requires the re-check; the tokens are the CMS-03C-12 ones (`pattern_depth_exceeded`, `pattern_nodes_exceeded`), ordered after `nested_pattern_not_active` in the provider precedence; placement answers 422 `pattern_depth_exceeded` at `/patternId` for a 9th level. BE03c 1585, 388 and changelog amended.
- **Downstream**: lane db10 (anchored-replacement migrations for cms_pattern_live_pin_reason / cms_pattern_active_digest / cms_pattern_placement_plan, contracts reason tokens, preflight copy); AC-211 c1.
- **Reversibility**: High

title: DEC-248: Refutation-9 database rulings on AC-294, AC-190, AC-044 and the definition lever (2026-10-31)
text:
- **Problem**: refute9db section 9 asked five rulings before the db9a/db9b rows can be applied.
- **Options considered**: per item, the strict reading (hold until proven) vs the contingent narrower reading the refuter offered.
- **Decision** (root, owner may override): (1) db9a U1 (real CMS-03A-17 revocation, the create waits at position 1) is cited under AC-294 part "authority/"; (2) AC-190 "selectors)" is plural: both the taxonomy and the pattern selector owner predicates must be isolated — held until the matched-pair test exists (lane db9a, a labelled clone made active through the real governed chain is acceptable fixture state for proving a READ filter; DEC-245(7) governs stand-in producers in concurrency, not read fixtures); (3) AC-044 "deletion" includes entry and owner deletion, which have no writer before Slice 16: held, the limitation names the proven pattern-source rows and the BOUNDARY; (4) the definition lock lever is judged on CMS-03B-10 itself: the create names contentTypeId/contentTypeVersionId, so the lever is reachable and needs the two missed tests (command and helper level, lane db9a); the CMS-03A-04 / CMS-03C-06 lever rows stay as passing tests without a Slice 12 citation; (5) the db9b RED suite runs in canonical gates only after the DEC-247 WIP is promoted (it then passes), and its [RED] markers are retitled as regression tests.
- **Downstream**: apply9; AC-294, AC-190, AC-108, AC-044 limitations; lane db9a follow-up.
- **Reversibility**: High

source: phase-2 slice-12 root (lane db9a follow-up item 5)
title: DEC-249: Forged fixture rows may prove a read filter, never a producer (2026-10-31)
text:
- **Problem**: DEC-248(2) allowed a labelled clone made active through the REAL governed chain to prove the CMS-03C-13 / nestable-read owner predicate; the real chain refuses it (cms_pattern_blocks_compatible requires the content type of the same owner), so lane db9a walked the clone active through the guarded lifecycle seam, labelled as a forgery.
- **Options considered**: (a) accept the forged row for the read-filter clauses (AC-108 c3, AC-190 c2) when the test also proves sensitivity (the same read with only the owner predicate removed lists it) and the owner positive control; (b) keep both clauses partial as BOUNDARY because no production producer can create the row.
- **Decision** (root, owner may override): (a). The clause claims a property of the READ ("never listed"); the row being unreachable makes the predicate defence in depth, not untestable. A forged fixture row is acceptable evidence for a read filter only with a labelled forgery, a predicate-removal sensitivity arm and an owner positive control; it is never acceptable for a producer, lock-order or concurrency claim (DEC-245(7) stands).
- **Downstream**: refute9 judges the db9c rows under this rule; AC-108, AC-190.
- **Reversibility**: High
